title: The String Library
summary: string.h has strlen, strcmp, strchr, strstr and memcpy. Copying and joining text safely means knowing the buffer size - snprintf is the safe tool, while strcpy and strcat trust you. ctype.h classifies and converts characters, and strtol turns text into numbers and tells you where it stopped.

cards.q: Why is snprintf safer than strcpy and strcat?
cards.a:
It is told the buffer size and never writes past it

It also always adds the terminator.

A pointer to the '=' inside the string

`strchr` returns a pointer into the string, or NULL when the character is not there.
